themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency Surge
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, Crown Heights residents filed 6 new tree requests (vs. 0.2 weekly average) and 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints (vs. 0.5 weekly average)—a combined 2,300% spike in new requests and 900% spike in maintenance complaints—suggesting either storm damage, seasonal growth, or a coordinated community mobilization around neglected green infrastructure.
evidence: New Tree Request complaints: 6 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, +2,300%)
Overgrown Tree/Branches complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.36, +900%)
Combined signal: 11 tree-related 311 complaints in one week vs. historical baseline of ~0.7 weekly
reporting_angles: Did a recent storm damage trees across Crown Heights/Prospect Heights, triggering resident complaints?
Is Parks Department maintenance falling behind in this district—and are residents now forced to file 311 complaints to force action?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance Crisis in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, maintenance or facility complaints jumped to 25 filings vs. 4.9 weekly average—a 413% spike (z-score: 9.13)—indicating widespread building system failures, possibly tied to aging infrastructure or landlord neglect across the district.
evidence: Maintenance or Facility complaints: 25 THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.13, +413%)
Context: Heat/Hot Water complaints remain second-highest 311 complaint type overall (2,215 in 90 days), suggesting heating systems are a chronic issue
Elevator complaints also spiked THIS WEEK: 3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average (+700%, z-score: 5.42)
reporting_angles: What triggered the spike in building maintenance complaints this week? Are landlords ignoring repair requests?
How many Crown Heights buildings have open violations for heating/plumbing/elevator systems, and what enforcement tools does DOB have?

themes_detail.label: Homelessness Assistance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: THREE WEEKS AGO (most recent data), homeless person assistance complaints spiked 643% to 26 filings vs. 3.5 weekly average (z-score: 10.61)—the highest z-score in the dataset—aligning with longstanding CB budget requests for expanded street outreach and homeless facilities, signaling either a surge in street homelessness or systemic service gaps.
evidence: Homeless Person Assistance complaints: 26 three weeks ago vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.61, +643%, highest z-score in dataset)
Convergence: Community Board budget requests include 'Expand street outreach' and 'Other facilities for homeless requests' to DHS—year-over-year repeating requests indicate chronic unmet need
CB also budgets repeatedly for 'Assign additional building inspectors'—suggesting housing stock deterioration may be driving both homelessness and maintenance complaints
reporting_angles: Where are homeless encampments concentrated in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights, and what services are residents calling 311 to request?
Has DHS responded to the spike in assistance requests 3 weeks ago? What outreach expansion is actually happening on the ground?

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Risk Spike
themes_detail.summary: TWO WEEKS AGO, lead-related complaints jumped to 11 filings vs. 3.6 weekly average—a 203% spike (z-score: 4.93)—potentially signaling increased awareness of lead in aging housing stock or new violations discovered during building inspections, a public health concern especially acute in Crown Heights.
evidence: Lead complaints: 11 two weeks ago vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.93, +203%)
Context: Paint/Plaster complaints are 6th-highest category overall (437 in 90 days)—consistent with older housing stock vulnerable to lead paint
CB budget requests 'Assign additional building inspectors' year-over-year, suggesting inspection capacity is strained
reporting_angles: Are recent lead violations clustered in specific Crown Heights neighborhoods? What do DOH records show about lead remediation timelines?
How many children in this district have been screened for lead exposure, and what support is available for families in contaminated housing?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicle Backlog
themes_detail.summary: LAST WEEK, abandoned vehicle complaints reached 17 filings vs. 5.9 weekly average—a 189% spike (z-score: 5.18)—suggesting either enforcement lags or a new cohort of derelict vehicles, a visible quality-of-life concern in the district.
evidence: Abandoned Vehicle complaints: 17 last week vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.18, +189%)
Context: Illegal Parking is the #1 complaint type overall (2,263 in 90 days), indicating street management is strained
Data is one week old; unclear if spike is sustained or temporary
reporting_angles: Which streets in Crown Heights have the most abandoned vehicles? Is NYPD removing them within the 30-day legal window?
Are residents having difficulty reporting abandoned vehicles, or is the city slow to process removal requests?
